title: Observability panorama - metrics map and trace annotations (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working, high-level map that ties together a small set of operational signals (metrics + traces) we think are essential for fast investigation of token-serving regressions and routing/fallback behavior. The goal is to produce: a compact canonical metric table, trace annotation conventions, and a minimal dashboard wireframe that an oncall or engineer can use to answer the 6 quick questions when a user reports slow or degraded responses.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus: token-serving path (API gateway -> router -> model runtime -> KV cache -> network) for hosted + dedicated.
- Excludes: batch offline training jobs, prefetch/embeddings pipelines (handled separately).
- Keep cardinality small for default dashboards (tenant, model, route) and provide guidance for deeper queries.
- Sampling: default light-traces + heavy-traces for anomalous requests (see tracing strategy).

Quick investigative questions cross-check (what dashboards should answer in <10m):
1) Is the issue client-side, network, or our runtime?
2) Which tenant(s) and model(s) are impacted?
3) Is latency due to token generation (CPU/GPU), KV-cache misses, or scheduling/backpressure?
4) Is there an increase in error rate, partial replies, or truncated streams?
5) Are fallbacks/variant-switches happening? (e.g., downgraded quantized model)
6) Did a recent rollout or autoscale change align with the onset?

Canonical metric table (compact; each row = primary signal we want instrumented):
- name: request.count
  owner: edge-team
  type: counter
  calculation: increment on API request accepted (post-auth)
  labels: tenant_id, route, model_id, region, plan
  sline: N/A (raw traffic)
  why: baseline traffic, sudden surges, lat spikes
  instrumentation: expose as prometheus counter with delta per minute

- name: request.latency.p50/p95/p99
  owner: serving-runtime
  type: histogram (bucketed)
  calculation: end_time - start_time (request lifecycle)
  labels: tenant_id, route, model_id, hardware_tier
  sli: p95 < 300ms (hosted default), p99 < 800ms
  why: latency attribution and SLOs
  notes: record path-level durations: gateway, routing, queuing, model-step

- name: token.gen.time.avg
  owner: serving-runtime
  type: gauge (per-request average)
  calculation: total_model_generation_time / tokens_generated
  labels: model_variant, seq_len_bucket
  sli: track regressions rather than fixed thresholds (baseline per model)
  why: isolates per-token cost and GPU execution regressions
  notes: ensure precise start/stop around model forward passes

- name: kvcache.hit_rate
  owner: kvcache-service
  type: ratio
  calculation: hits / (hits + misses) over 1m window
  labels: tenant_id, model_id, prefix_len_bucket
  sli: expected > 0.75 for long-form chat tenants (tunable)
  why: cache-sensitivity -> huge cost/latency impact
  notes: expose both per-tenant and global rollups

- name: scheduler.queue_depth / scheduler.queue_time
  owner: platform-scheduler
  type: gauge / histogram
  calculation: instantaneous queue length; time spent waiting for scheduling
  labels: node_pool, hardware_tier, tenant_priority
  sli: p95 queue_time < 80ms for dedicated pools
  why: reveals throttling or burst backpressure

- name: fallback.invocations
  owner: routing-service
  type: counter
  calculation: increment when request is routed to fallback model/region
  labels: tenant_id, route, fallback_reason
  sli: track spike events; no hard SLO (alert on >10x baseline)
  why: indicates capacity failure modes or canary regressions
  notes: include original_model_id and fallback_model_id in trace attributes

- name: response.error_rate / partial_response_rate
  owner: api-gateway
  type: ratio
  calculation: non-2xx / total requests; partial responses flagged by stream_close_reason != success
  labels: tenant_id, route, model_id
  sli: p95 < 0.5% (hosted baseline)
  why: user-visible disruption

- name: infra.gpu.utilization / infra.gpu.temperature
  owner: infra
  type: gauge
  calculation: average utilization across serving pods per pool
  labels: node_pool, model_id, instance_type
  why: hardware hotspots and thermal throttling signals

Tracing conventions (minimal, consistent):
- top-level span: request:<tenant_id>:<route> (duration = full request lifecycle)
  - attributes: tenant_id, route, model_id, request_id, client_sdk, api_key_hash
- child spans (ordered):
  - gateway.auth (time to auth + validate)
  - router.resolve (policy routing, variant selection)
    attributes: policy_id, matched_capacity_tier, chosen_variant, fallback_reason(optional)
  - scheduler.enqueue (time in queue), scheduler.dispatch
    attributes: queue_position, node_pool, preemption_flag
  - model.exec (split into warmup/kvcache/apply-kv/forward/backward-style-notes if relevant)
    attributes: seq_len, tokens_requested, tokens_returned, kvcache_hit_boolean, quantization_profile
  - streaming.flusher (time to first-byte and time to last-byte for streaming responses)
  - fallback.transition spans when a fallback is attempted

Span naming guidance: keep names short, use dot-separated lower-case, include boolean attributes rather than long names in parenthesis. Example: router.resolve, model.exec.kv_hit, model.exec.forward.

Sampling strategy (pragmatic default):
- keep 1% baseline full-traces across all traffic for trend analysis
- always keep traces for: requests with latency > p99, failed requests, fallback.invocations events, and any request that touches a canary model or new rollout flag
- for heavy tenants (top 5 by traffic), keep 5% sample to improve attribution
- apply reservoir sampling in collectors to preserve head/tail variety

Trace attribute redaction rules:
- never include PII: email, phone, raw prompt content (except when explicitly authorized for evals)
- include prompt hash (sha256 truncated) + tokens_returned + user_context_age_bucket as safe indexed attributes

Dashboard wireframe notes (minimal pages):
1) Overview (ops-at-a-glance):
   - panels: global traffic heatmap, p95 latency by region, error rate trend, fallback rate trend, active canary flags
   - quick filters: tenant, model, region, time-window (1h/6h/24h)
2) Latency decomposition (investigation):
   - panels: waterfall breakdown (gateway | routing | queue | model.exec), token.gen.time churn by seq_len bucket, queue depth by node_pool
   - drill link: open trace for top slow requests (link to trace viewer with request_id)
3) Cache health & economics (cost sensitivity):
   - panels: kvcache.hit_rate by tenant, miss latency histogram, cost-per-token estimate by cache hit/miss
4) Fallback & rollout incidents:
   - panels: fallback.invocations over time, map of which variants served most, canary alignment timeline, correlated deploy events (from linked_artifacts)
5) Topology & capacity (SRE):
   - panels: pool utilization, GPU temperature, upcoming scheduled maintenance, autoscale decisions (events table)

Widget heuristics:
- limit top-N cardinality (top 10) by default, with a query link to full table
- pre-aggregate p95/p99 at ingestion for common time buckets to reduce query cost
- annotate dashboards with deploy IDs + rollout tags (pull from routing-service events)

Alerting guidance (cheap + actionable):
- p95 latency increase by >30% vs 1h rolling baseline for 5m -> warning; 60% -> critical
- request.error_rate > 2% absolute and sustained for 10m -> pager if >1k rps or if affecting a high-priority tenant
- fallback.invocations rate spike > 5x baseline in 1m -> pager for SRE
- kvcache.hit_rate drop > 20% for >10m -> page owner of tenant or platform depending on scope

Investigation play (step-by-step checklist):
1) Use Overview page, filter by tenant or region mentioned in report
2) If p95 elevated, open Latency decomposition and check queue_time vs model.exec contribution
3) Jump to traces for p99 requests (link from widget). Confirm if kvcache_hit_boolean is false or quantization slowed forward()
4) Check fallback.invocations timeline and compare with deploy events (JIRA/PR link)
5) If infra signals (gpu.util high, node_pool saturated), escalate to infra on-call with node_pool + top-affected model list
6) Add a short blameless note in ongoing incident doc and flag metric owners to instrument missing attributes

Operational notes and short-term action items (TODO list):
- [ ] Add tokens_returned and prompt_hash to all request spans (tracking in OBS-1987)
- [ ] Ingest p95/p99 at 1m rollups to reduce slow queries (infra quota request: TELEM-298)
- [ ] Create dashboard template that auto-injects latest canary tags from routing-service events
- [ ] Automate trace sampling boost for new model rollouts (hook into rollout service)
- [ ] Draft short runbook for fallback storms (owner: routing-service)

Open questions / debates (notes to self):
- Do we compute token.gen.time per model shard or per hardware tier? (affects cardinality)
- How aggressively should we sample prompt hashes for evals vs privacy? Need cross-team legal signoff for raw prompt retention
- Should fallback.invocations include a field for observed quality delta (post-hoc eval)? Might be heavy but useful

References and quick links:
- Confluence: OBS-PANORAMA-42 (telemetry spec stub)
- Jira: OBS-1987 (trace attr rollout)
- GitHub: redwood-infra/telemetry#412 (collection sampler update)

Appendix: example prometheus queries (sketches)
- p95 latency by route:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- kv cache hit rate (1m):
  sum(rate(kvcache_hits_total[1m])) by (tenant_id) / sum(rate(kvcache_hits_total[1m]) + rate(kvcache_misses_total[1m])) by (tenant_id)

End notes:
This document should stay slim. The objective is to converge on a small set of stable labels and tracing anchors such that dashboards are cheap and investigations are reproducible. Will iterate once we have initial instrumentation PRs merged.

---
Notes to self: sync with priya next week to validate tenant-level SLOs and confirm sampling budget with infra.
